evidence.title: Reinforcement Learning-Based Adaptive Wire Gauge Selection for Zonal Automotive Harness Design Under Dynamic Driving Scenarios
evidence.abstract: This paper presents a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for adaptive wire–gauge selection in zonal automotive wiring harnesses under dynamic driving scenarios. Focusing on the centroid–to–battery (pre-distribution) segment, the method minimizes conductor mass while enforcing electrical constraints: a voltage–drop limit of 0.36 V (3% of 12 V) and temperature–aware ampacity. Scenario–dependent current profiles are derived from a zonal dataset with four representative operating conditions; distances and topology are held fixed, and only wire types are optimized. A multi–head Deep Q–Network (DQN) selects a gauge per centroid using a reward that balances mass reduction, constraint compliance, and voltage–budget utilization. Validation with MATLAB scripts and a companion Simulink model shows near–identical voltage drops, margins, and validity flags across 65°C, 85°C, and 105°C. On a 12–zone High–application case at 85°C, the RL policy achieves 100% compliance with an average voltage drop of 0.30 V, whereas baselines (a static–gauge design from Hossain et al. and a rule–based scenario–aware method) exhibit higher drops and lower compliance. System–level comparisons with Hossain et al. (distances unchanged) indicate total harness mass reductions of –3.62% (Low), –32.01% (Mid), and –34.51% (High). For the 12–zone High case, the RL design reduces centroid $\to $ battery mass by 12.52 kg, yielding about €108.13 copper cost savings (priced at € 8.6338/kg) and 51.95 kg CO2e lower embodied emissions per harness. Results demonstrate that scenario–aware RL provides a practical, scalable path to lighter, standard–compliant harnesses that remain robust across temperatures and load variability.

evidence.title: Automatic cable harness layout routing in a customizable 3D environment
evidence.abstract: Designing cable harnesses can be time-consuming and complex due to many design and manufacturing aspects and rules. Automating the design process can help to fulfil these rules, speed up the process, and optimize the design. To accommodate this, we formulate a harness routing optimization problem to minimize cable lengths, maximize bundling by rewarding shared paths, and optimize the cables' spatial location with respect to case-specific information of the routing environment, e.g., zones to avoid. A deterministic and computationally effective cable harness routing algorithm has been developed to solve the routing problem and is used to generate a set of cable harness topology candidates and approximate the Pareto front. Our approach was tested against a stochastic and an exact solver and our routing algorithm generated objective function values better than the stochastic approach and close to the exact solver. Our algorithm was able to find solutions, some of them being proven to be near-optimal, for three industrial-sized 3D cases within reasonable time (in magnitude of seconds to minutes) and the computation times were comparable to those of the stochastic approach.

evidence.title: A Strategy for Power System Stability Improvement via Controlled Charge/Discharge of Plug-in Electric Vehicles
evidence.abstract: Plug-in electrical vehicles (PEV) are capable of both grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) power transfer. The advantages of developing V2G include an additional revenue stream for cleaner vehicles, increased stability and reliability of the electric grid, lower electric system costs, and eventually, inexpensive storage and backup for renewable electricity. Here we show how smart control of PEVs can improve the stability of power grids using only local frequency measurements. We evaluate the proposed control strategy on the IEEE Case 3 and the IEEE New England power systems. The results show that V2G leads to improved steady-state stability, larger region of stability, reduced frequency and voltage fluctuations during transients and longer critical clearing times.

evidence.title: Dynamic State Estimation for Integrated Natural Gas and Electric Power Systems
evidence.abstract: A dynamic state estimation method of integrated natural gas and electric power systems (IGESs) in proposed. Firstly, the coupling model of gas pipeline networks and power systems by gas turbine units (GTUs) is established. Secondly, the Kalman filter based linear DSE model for the IGES is built. The gas density and mass flow rate, as well as the real and imaginary parts of bus voltages are taken as states, which are predicted by the linearized fluid dynamic equations of gases and exponential smoothing techniques. Boundary conditions of pipeline networks are used as supplementary constraints in the system model. At last, the proposed method is applied to an IGES including a 30-node pipeline network and IEEE 39-bus system coupled by two GTUs. Two indexes are used to evaluate the DSE performance under three measurement error conditions, and the results show that the DSE can obtain the accurate dynamic states in different conditions.

evidence.abstract: This paper presents the development of a tool for automatic analysis and evaluation of vehicle electrical and electronic systems projects based on data science, in order to detect and suggest optimization opportunities related to cost, weight and efficiency of the electrical distribution circuits of developed or under development projects. On the cost side of vehicular electrical distribution cabling, the project has the potential to bring a great financial return, as it is not uncommon for the responsible company, be it the supplier or Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), to err on the side of caution and oversize the project. evidence.title: Intermittency phenomena in electrical connectors
evidence.abstract: Fretting is known to be a major cause of contact deterioration and failure, particularly in tin-plated contacts. During fretting the contact resistance generally increases slowly with time. Superimposed on this slow increase in contact resistance are rapid changes in contact resistance within fractions of a second, called intermittences or short duration discontinuities. Although intermittences have been reported by several authors, they are frequently overlooked in traditional fretting experiments and not much is known about their origin. The present study aims at filling this gap. A test apparatus has been built to measure the contact voltage-drop profile during an intermittence and fretting experiments on tin-plated copper contacts have been carried out. The results lead to a set of requirements for a model to explain intermittency phenomena

evidence.title: An Optimization Framework for the Design of Cable Harness Layouts in Planar Interconnected Systems
evidence.abstract: The components of complex systems such as automobiles or ships communicate via connectors, including wires, hoses, or pipes whose weight could substantially increase the total weight of the system. Hence, it is of paramount importance to lay out these connectors such that their overall weight is minimized. In this paper, a computationally efficient approach is proposed to optimize the layout of flexible connectors (e.g., cable harnesses) by minimizing their overall length while maximizing their common length. The approach provides a framework to mathematically model the cable harness layout optimization problem. A Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) solver is then applied to solve the optimization problem, which outputs a set of non-dominated solutions to the bi-objective problem. Finally, the effects of the workspace’s geometric structure on the optimal layouts of cable harnesses are discussed using sample test cases. The overarching objective of this study is to provide insight for designers of cable harnesses when deciding on the final layout of connectors considering aspects such as accessibility to and maintainability of these connectors.

system.value: A Strategy for Power System Stability Improvement via Controlled Charge/Discharge of Plug-in Electric Vehicles

abstract.value: Plug-in electrical vehicles (PEV) are capable of both grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) power transfer. The advantages of developing V2G include an additional revenue stream for cleaner vehicles, increased stability and reliability of the electric grid, lower electric system costs, and eventually, inexpensive storage and backup for renewable electricity. Here we show how smart control of PEVs can improve the stability of power grids using only local frequency measurements. We evaluate the proposed control strategy on the IEEE Case 3 and the IEEE New England power systems. The results show that V2G leads to improved steady-state stability, larger region of stability, reduced frequency and voltage fluctuations during transients and longer critical clearing times.

abstract.value: This paper presents the development of a tool for automatic analysis and evaluation of vehicle electrical and electronic systems projects based on data science, in order to detect and suggest optimization opportunities related to cost, weight and efficiency of the electrical distribution circuits of developed or under development projects. On the cost side of vehicular electrical distribution cabling, the project has the potential to bring a great financial return, as it is not uncommon for the responsible company, be it the supplier or Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), to err on the side of caution and oversize the project. This approach is often taken as a preventive measure to mitigate any potential design problems that may arise from a leaner design. Considering all challenges inherent to harness development process as electrical harnesses manufacturing complexity and the material amount that is often oversized in design, respecting all the development phases, it is recommended to develop an optimized electrical distribution tool.

A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

warnings.lesson:
FROZEN THEOREM CE-018: A novelty claim survives only when the candidate's CAPABILITY (what it can DO) is demonstrably absent from the prior art landscape — not when the candidate's KEYWORDS (what words it uses) are absent. The correct procedure: (1) decompose the candidate into its functional capabilities (e.g., 'intrapprocedural clot sensing' not 'retrieved-clot physical signature measurement'); (2) search the prior art landscape for each capability using the prior art's own vocabulary (assignee names, CPC classes, commercial product names, inventor terminology); (3) build a capability collision matrix mapping each capability to prior art coverage; (4) only if at least one capability is genuinely UNOCCUPIED (confirmed by both patent search AND commercial frontier analysis) can a novelty claim be recorded. Semantic re-skins (CE-012 violation) include: 'retrieved-clot' vs 'in-situ clot'; 'physical signature' vs 'composition'; 'integrated sensor' vs 'catheter-mounted sensor.' These distinctions prove nothing. The test is capability, not vocabulary.

SHARPENED (per CEO Round 62 audit): Capability novelty must be evaluated at the FUNCTIONAL END-TO-END level: input → inference → decision → physical effect → measurable outcome. Otherwise the machine can still find a 'novel' intermediate layer (e.g., a new sensor modality, a new feature, a new algorithm) that is already covered by an existing end-to-end system. The correct end-to-end test: (5) decompose the candidate into the complete causal loop — what is observed → what is inferred → what is predicted → what physical action becomes possible → what measurable outcome changes; (6) map each step of this loop to the prior art's end-to-end systems (not just individual capabilities); (7) only if the candidate's complete causal loop is demonstrably absent from the prior art's end-to-end systems can a novelty claim be recorded. A 'novel' intermediate layer that plugs into an existing end-to-end system is NOT novel — it is a substitution, not an invention. The unit of novelty is the complete causal loop, not the sensor, feature, algorithm, or capability.

informational.lesson: MODEL-BOUNDED NEGATIVE RESULT: Before inventing variable geometry, calculate absolute pressure-control authority at the actual operating point. Relative r^4 sensitivity is meaningless if the absolute pressure drop is tiny. Under realistic post-stenting conditions (D=5-10mm, Q=200-500 mL/min), adaptive diameter control of a venous sinus produces <0.2 mmHg change in AG gradient — 5x below the 1 mmHg pre-registered threshold. Control authority exists only in the stenotic+high-flow regime (D≤4mm, Q≥1200 mL/min), which is incompatible with a stented patient whose stent has normalized diameter to 7-10mm. The network model (1323 configs) confirms: flow redistribution through contralateral sinus does NOT rescue control authority (dominance has no effect). NOT a universal vascular invariant — based on Poiseuille model with specific assumptions about geometry, flow, and topology.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-019: A clinical-pathway-aware evidence selector must demonstrate that the clinical-pathway bridge produces a MATERIALLY DIFFERENT and BETTER evidence set than information-maximizing selection (BOED). If the pathway-aware selector uses MORE tests while achieving WORSE assurance, the clinical-pathway bridge adds complexity without value. The minimum-evidence claim must be validated by showing tests_required < BOED, not just tests_required < conventional. The killer experiment must compare against the STRONGEST available baseline (BOED), not just conventional full-validation.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-020: A sufficiency proof that is merely an integration of known statistical methods (NI testing + coverage + multiple-testing correction + sensitivity analysis) is NOT a novel mathematical result. Under §103, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is likely obvious (KSR v. Teleflex). The frontier is a NEW MATHEMATICAL BOUND — e.g., a tight bound on minimum evidence set size that is better than what existing methods give individually, or a proof technique that connects clinical pathway coverage to statistical sufficiency in a way that is not derivable from existing theory. Additionally: killer tests for sufficiency proofs must include a TRUE POSITIVE case (sufficient evidence for a SAFE modification that the system correctly accepts), not just a true negative (insufficient evidence that the system correctly rejects).

Under KSR, combining known methods to solve a problem the market explicitly asks for is obvious. The coder correctly identified this in the R254 ranking ("NI testing is standard, high collision risk") but incorrectly chose to proceed. The CEO corrected: high collision risk is a RED FLAG, not a reason to proceed. Kill immediately if the smallest surviving mechanism is standard statistics + ML context + automated reporting.

informational.mechanism: SGET (Strain-Gated Electrochemical Transduction) — A=strain pulse changes B=electrochemical sensor from 2D surface to 3D depth profiling. First synergy-2 candidate.
informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-022: Synergy ≠ novelty and synergy ≠ commercial moat. A functional interaction (A changes B) is NECESSARY but NOT SUFFICIENT for invention. The interaction itself — the causal law, the emergent effect, and functional equivalents across domains — must survive prior art independently. Additionally: synergy claims without quantitative comparison against the STRONGEST baseline are stories, not evidence. The unexpected-effect proof requires: (1) pre-registered quantitative prediction, (2) strongest baseline identified, (3) killer experiment vs that baseline, (4) result not predictable from A and B independently. The new standard: A changes B → unexpected effect → interaction survives prior art → reproducible advantage → cannot be cheaply reproduced → buyer value.

informational.lesson: FROZEN THEOREM CE-023: A candidate that survives the 14-gate protocol at the CONCEPT level can be killed at the ELEMENT-DECOMPOSITION level. The 14 gates assessed M4 against the broad concept (continuously renewing anti-biofilm surface) and found M4=NOT FOUND. custody_records.raw_content: This paper presents a reinforcement learning (RL) framework for adaptive wire–gauge selection in zonal automotive wiring harnesses under dynamic driving scenarios. Focusing on the centroid–to–battery (pre-distribution) segment, the method minimizes conductor mass while enforcing electrical constraints: a voltage–drop limit of 0.36 V (3% of 12 V) and temperature–aware ampacity. Scenario–dependent current profiles are derived from a zonal dataset with four representative operating conditions; distances and topology are held fixed, and only wire types are optimized. A multi–head Deep Q–Network (DQN) selects a gauge per centroid using a reward that balances mass reduction, constraint compliance, and voltage–budget utilization. Validation with MATLAB scripts and a companion Simulink model shows near–identical voltage drops, margins, and validity flags across 65°C, 85°C, and 105°C. On a 12–zone High–application case at 85°C, the RL policy achieves 100% compliance with an average voltage drop of 0.30 V, whereas baselines (a static–gauge design from Hossain et al. and a rule–based scenario–aware method) exhibit higher drops and lower compliance. System–level comparisons with Hossain et al. (distances unchanged) indicate total harness mass reductions of –3.62% (Low), –32.01% (Mid), and –34.51% (High). For the 12–zone High case, the RL design reduces centroid $\to $ battery mass by 12.52 kg, yielding about €108.13 copper cost savings (priced at € 8.6338/kg) and 51.95 kg CO2e lower embodied emissions per harness. Results demonstrate that scenario–aware RL provides a practical, scalable path to lighter, standard–compliant harnesses that remain robust across temperatures and load variability.

custody_records.raw_content: Designing cable harnesses can be time-consuming and complex due to many design and manufacturing aspects and rules. Automating the design process can help to fulfil these rules, speed up the process, and optimize the design. To accommodate this, we formulate a harness routing optimization problem to minimize cable lengths, maximize bundling by rewarding shared paths, and optimize the cables' spatial location with respect to case-specific information of the routing environment, e.g., zones to avoid. A deterministic and computationally effective cable harness routing algorithm has been developed to solve the routing problem and is used to generate a set of cable harness topology candidates and approximate the Pareto front. Our approach was tested against a stochastic and an exact solver and our routing algorithm generated objective function values better than the stochastic approach and close to the exact solver. Our algorithm was able to find solutions, some of them being proven to be near-optimal, for three industrial-sized 3D cases within reasonable time (in magnitude of seconds to minutes) and the computation times were comparable to those of the stochastic approach.

The advantages of developing V2G include an additional revenue stream for cleaner vehicles, increased stability and reliability of the electric grid, lower electric system costs, and eventually, inexpensive storage and backup for renewable electricity. Here we show how smart control of PEVs can improve the stability of power grids using only local frequency measurements. We evaluate the proposed control strategy on the IEEE Case 3 and the IEEE New England power systems. The results show that V2G leads to improved steady-state stability, larger region of stability, reduced frequency and voltage fluctuations during transients and longer critical clearing times.

Firstly, the coupling model of gas pipeline networks and power systems by gas turbine units (GTUs) is established. Secondly, the Kalman filter based linear DSE model for the IGES is built. The gas density and mass flow rate, as well as the real and imaginary parts of bus voltages are taken as states, which are predicted by the linearized fluid dynamic equations of gases and exponential smoothing techniques. Boundary conditions of pipeline networks are used as supplementary constraints in the system model. At last, the proposed method is applied to an IGES including a 30-node pipeline network and IEEE 39-bus system coupled by two GTUs. Two indexes are used to evaluate the DSE performance under three measurement error conditions, and the results show that the DSE can obtain the accurate dynamic states in different conditions.

During fretting the contact resistance generally increases slowly with time. Superimposed on this slow increase in contact resistance are rapid changes in contact resistance within fractions of a second, called intermittences or short duration discontinuities. Although intermittences have been reported by several authors, they are frequently overlooked in traditional fretting experiments and not much is known about their origin. The present study aims at filling this gap. custody_records.raw_content: The components of complex systems such as automobiles or ships communicate via connectors, including wires, hoses, or pipes whose weight could substantially increase the total weight of the system. Hence, it is of paramount importance to lay out these connectors such that their overall weight is minimized. In this paper, a computationally efficient approach is proposed to optimize the layout of flexible connectors (e.g., cable harnesses) by minimizing their overall length while maximizing their common length. The approach provides a framework to mathematically model the cable harness layout optimization problem. A Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm (MOGA) solver is then applied to solve the optimization problem, which outputs a set of non-dominated solutions to the bi-objective problem. Finally, the effects of the workspace’s geometric structure on the optimal layouts of cable harnesses are discussed using sample test cases. The overarching objective of this study is to provide insight for designers of cable harnesses when deciding on the final layout of connectors considering aspects such as accessibility to and maintainability of these connectors.
